That triggers JsonSchema constructor which expects ValidationContext not null? The stack trace shows JsonSchema.<init> uses validationContext.getMetaSchema(). So need to provide a mock ValidationContext with stub getMetaSchema returning something (maybe null). Simplify: Instead of extending JsonSchema, we could use a stub subclass that bypasses super constructor? But JsonSchema has protected constructor requiring many params. In our MutableJsonSchema we called super(null,null,null,null,null). That's causing NPE because validationContext null. Could pass a dummy ValidationContext implementation that returns null for getMetaSchema and others. Create a simple stub class implementing ValidationContext interface (need to see methods). Not provided. Could use Mockito? Not allowed. Simpler: Use a concrete subclass of JsonSchema that overrides needed methods and does not call super? But must call super. Maybe JsonSchema has another constructor that takes less args? Not known. Could avoid using JsonSchema subclass at all: parentSchemaProvider could return mockParentSchema from setup (MutableJsonSchema) that already constructed with a valid ValidationContext. So we need a valid ValidationContext instance for constructing JsonSchema. Could create a minimal implementation: class DummyValidationContext implements ValidationContext { public JsonMetaSchema getMetaSchema() { return null; } ... other methods maybe required. Need to look at interface. Not given. Might be many methods. Alternative: Use null parent schema in parameterized test? But test expects injection of parent schema and verify same reference. Could just use the same mockParentSchema (created in setup) which is a MutableJsonSchema constructed with a DummyValidationContext. So we need to create DummyValidationContext and use it in setup and provider.

Simplify: In setup, create a DummyValidationContext instance and pass to constructors. In provider, create new MutableJsonSchema with same dummy context.

Implement DummyValidationContext implements ValidationContext with minimal methods returning null or defaults. Need to import ValidationContext. We'll implement all abstract methods? Not sure number. Might be many. Could instead avoid using JsonSchema subclass and use a simple stub that extends JsonSchema but overrides constructor to not call super? Not possible.

Maybe easier: Instead of using JsonSchema subclass, we can use a mock via Mockito, but not allowed? Could add Mockito dependency? The original code had commented @Mock annotations. Could use MockitoAnnotations.initMocks(this) in @BeforeEach. Provide mockParentSchema = mock(JsonSchema.class); mockValidationContext = mock(ValidationContext.class); when(mockValidationContext.getMetaSchema()).thenReturn(null); That would avoid NPE. Use Mockito. Likely project includes Mockito. We'll add imports and initMocks.

Thus modify setupBeforeEach: annotate @BeforeEach, call MockitoAnnotations.openMocks(this); create mocks with Mockito.mock.

Remove MutableJsonSchema class? Could keep but not needed. But provider needs JsonSchema instances; we can use mock(JsonSchema.class) for each. Provide two distinct mocks.

Thus no need for MutableJsonSchema. Remove that class or keep but not used.

- Annotate class with @ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)

- Uncomment @Mock annotations on fields.

- Uncomment @BeforeEach annotation on setupBeforeEach.

- In provider, use mock(JsonSchema.class) via Mockito.mock.

- Remove usage of mockParentSchema? Keep.

- Ensure mockValidatorType not null; we can keep as ValidatorTypeCode.TYPE.

- Ensure mockValidationContext not null; we need mock it: @Mock ValidationContext mockValidationContext; Also stub getMetaSchema maybe not needed because not used in validator? But JsonSchema constructor may call validationContext.getMetaSchema(). In TestValidator constructor super(...). BaseJsonValidator likely doesn't use validationContext directly. However JsonSchema constructor (for parent schema) may be called when we create mockParentSchema? But mockParentSchema is a mock, not actual JsonSchema instance, so its constructor not invoked. So fine.

Thus parentSchemaProvider returns mock(JsonSchema.class) instances.
